title: Sales and marketing strategy: One plan, one data layer
summary: Create a sales and marketing strategy plan on a shared data layer that preserves buyer activity, campaign history, handoffs, pipeline, and revenue feedback.
body_markdown:
## Sales and marketing strategy: One plan, one data layer


Monday's alignment meeting goes well. Marketing shares the campaign, sales agrees with the target accounts, and revenue operations confirms the routing rules. By Thursday, the campaign platform, website, and CRM show three versions of the same account; sales cannot see which proof the buyer read, while marketing cannot tell whether the lead was rejected or merely reassigned.


Intentions aligned in the meeting. The operating system did not.


A sales and marketing strategy needs a shared market thesis and a shared representation of the buyer journey. One data layer does not mean one enormous application. It means the people, accounts, interactions, assets, campaigns, handoffs, opportunities, and outcomes remain connected well enough for both teams to act on the same reality.


## Sales and marketing strategy summary


In practice, a sales and marketing strategy defines the market the company will pursue, the problem and offer it will lead with, how demand will be created and captured, how sales will continue the interaction, and how pipeline and revenue will improve future work. The plan becomes operable through shared definitions, linked data, clear ownership, governed workflows, and a common scorecard.


Keep the CRM as the commercial system of record, the CMS as the publishing system, and the marketing automation platform as the messaging engine. The shared layer should resolve identity and relationships across them, preserve context, and return outcomes to the decisions that created the journey.

## A sales and marketing strategy needs one market thesis


Sales and marketing alignment is often reduced to lead definitions and service levels. Those controls come after a more consequential agreement: which market, buying situation, problem, offer, and evidence deserve coordinated investment.


Write the thesis as a decision record both teams can challenge. Include the target and excluded segments, triggering conditions, buyer roles, costly status quo, current alternative, promised change, approved proof, commercial motion, and evidence that would cause a revision. Sales should see its account experience in the thesis. Marketing should be able to turn it into content, campaigns, and conversion paths.


Surface's existing guide to[sales and marketing strategy for an internal audience](https://www.withsurface.com/blog/sales-and-marketing-strategy-why-content-needs-an-internal) explains why enablement should be treated as part of content strategy. A buyer-facing claim that sales cannot explain or support is an operating liability. A repeated sales objection that never reaches content leaves the next buyer to discover the same gap.


## Build a sales and marketing strategy on shared objects


Start by representing the business questions the plan needs to answer. Durable objects and explicit relationships are more useful than a collection of dashboard fields.


Shared object Context it should preserve Decisions it supports


Person Identity, role, consent, activity, requests, and account relationships Communication, qualification, follow-up, and experience


Account Firmographics, ownership, segment, fit, technology, active initiatives, and history Targeting, territory, coverage, route, and investment


Interaction Source, channel, timestamp, content, action, and confidence Journey analysis, intent interpretation, and response


Asset Topic, audience, claim, evidence, format, owner, version, and publish state Content reuse, governance, performance, and decay


Campaign Objective, market, message, offer, assets, channels, cost, and dates Coordination, measurement, and budget


Handoff Qualification basis, route, owner, context, timing, acceptance, and rejection Operations, capacity, service levels, and repair


Opportunity Stakeholders, product, stage, value, source context, objections, and movement Pipeline, forecast, proof, and sales learning


Outcome Accepted, rejected, won, lost, retained, expanded, and reason Targeting, messaging, routing, product, and strategy


One object may live primarily in one system. The requirement is that identifiers and definitions let the team connect it to the rest of the journey. Document which system owns each field, which workflows may update it, how conflicts resolve, and which changes require human approval.


## Turn the data layer into a sales and marketing strategy plan


Four operating parts make a sales and marketing strategy plan useful. The market plan defines the thesis, account universe, buying situations, offers, and coverage. The campaign plan turns those choices into messages, evidence, assets, distribution, and conversion actions. The handoff plan defines qualification, routing, ownership, response, recycle, and feedback. The measurement plan establishes the journey states, cohorts, scorecard, evidence labels, and decision cadence.


Connect every plan item to a shared object and an owner. If the company chooses a new segment, identify which account rules, campaigns, briefs, forms, routes, sales plays, and reports must change. If sales reports an objection, connect it to the relevant segment, opportunity, claim, asset, and content owner. This is how an insight becomes maintained context instead of meeting residue.

The two experiences become more useful when they share the same account and outcome definitions.


## A practical sales alignment example


Suppose marketing sees high engagement from regional fintech platforms and proposes a compliance-readiness campaign. Sales agrees that the accounts fit but says deals are stalling during security review. Revenue operations finds that the existing form routes technical review requests to the general inbound queue.


In a connected plan, the team links the target segment to the campaign, adds approved security evidence to the core asset and sales play, changes the form path for review requests, routes them to the right specialist, and records whether the meeting advances the opportunity. If the segment engages but qualified opportunities still stall for the same reason, the product or implementation plan may need attention. Better copy cannot solve a missing capability.


This sales alignment example works because the teams share the objects and outcome. Nobody needs to claim that one asset caused the sale. They can observe the journey, inspect the handoff, and decide whether evidence, operations, product, or targeting is the current constraint.


## Govern the shared layer without creating a new silo


Shared data can spread errors faster if ownership is vague. Establish field-level sources of truth, deduplication rules, retention and consent policies, access controls, confidence labels, audit history, and exception handling. Give a person authority to repair the model when automation encounters ambiguity.

Based on 1,015 marketers, the 2026 Content Marketing Institute and MarketingProfs[B2B research](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/b2b-research/b2b-content-marketing-trends-research) found that effective teams frequently credited customer understanding, sales alignment, measurement, content quality, and team capability. A shared data layer gives the teams a place to preserve and apply what they learn from those disciplines.


## Let revenue update the sales marketing strategy


Close the loop with a small, consistent outcome vocabulary and useful reasons. Accepted and rejected handoffs should improve qualification and routes. Opportunity movement should sharpen proof and sales plays. Wins and losses should challenge the market thesis, content priorities, offers, and channel investment.

People still judge whether a pattern is meaningful and approve consequential changes. The system makes the evidence available where the next action happens.


One plan and one data layer will not remove functional expertise. Marketing still understands markets, messages, and demand. Sales still understands live buying situations and commercial progress. The shared layer lets those perspectives accumulate instead of resetting at every handoff.
